# infrawrench_sso_settings (Resource)

How members sign in to the organization through enterprise single sign-on (SAML or OIDC through WorkOS), and how SCIM Directory Sync provisions them.

The identity provider connection, the directory and domain verification are configured by your IT admin in the WorkOS Admin Portal, opened from **Settings → Single Sign-On**; a provider cannot drive that flow. This resource owns what Infrawrench decides: whether SSO is enforced, who the break-glass owners are, and whether the directory may change membership. Creating it sets SSO up for the organization if it was not already.

Turning `enforce_sso` on is refused by the server unless a domain is verified, a connection is active, at least one break-glass owner is listed, and the credential applying it would still be let in. With an API key that means its owner must be a break-glass owner (or sit outside the enforced domains). The key needs the `org:settings:write` scope, and the organization must be on the paid plan.

An organization **singleton** with no DELETE on the route: `terraform destroy` leaves the settings exactly as configured. Removing this resource does not quietly switch enforcement off, which is the safer default for a sign-in control.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The identity provider and directory are connected by your IT admin in the
# WorkOS Admin Portal (Settings -> Single Sign-On). This holds the decisions.
resource "infrawrench_sso_settings" "this" {
  # Refused by the server until a domain is verified, a connection is active
  # and at least one break-glass owner is listed.
  enforce_sso = true

  # Owners who can still get in when the identity provider is down.
  break_glass_user_ids = ["user_01HXYZABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWX"]

  provisioning_enabled = true
  auto_add_seats       = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `auto_add_seats` (Boolean) Buy a seat when provisioning needs one. Off, members past the seat count wait instead of growing the bill. Turning it on also needs `billing:write`.
- `break_glass_user_ids` (List of String) User ids of owners who may still sign in without SSO when the identity provider is down. Each must be a current owner; at most 5. At least one is required while `enforce_sso` is true. Every bypass is audit-logged.
- `enforce_sso` (Boolean) Require members whose email is in a verified domain to sign in through the organization's identity provider. Existing non-SSO sessions stop working for them in this organization. API keys are not affected.
- `provisioning_enabled` (Boolean) Let Directory Sync add and remove members. Off, the directory is only observed, so mappings can be previewed before it changes anything.

### Optional

- `default_role_id` (String) Role for provisioned members none of whose groups is mapped. Omit for the system member role. Never the owner role.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The organization id. Single sign-on is an organization singleton, so this is the only value it ever takes and it is what `terraform import` addresses.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# An organization singleton: there is only ever one, and it has no id of its
# own, so it imports under the organization id.
terraform import infrawrench_sso_settings.this org_01HXYZABCDEF
```
